source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֖י גֹּ֑מֶר אַשְׁכֲּנַ֥ז וְ/דִיפַ֖ת וְ/תוֹגַרְמָֽה׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz[a], Diphath, and Togarmah.

signals.text: Genesis 10:3 reads 'Riphath' in the parallel genealogy; here the Hebrew text of Chronicles reads 'Diphath.'

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֥י יָוָ֖ן אֱלִישָׁ֣ה וְ/תַרְשִׁ֑ישָׁ/ה כִּתִּ֖ים וְ/רוֹדָנִֽים׃ס
english_snapshot: And the sons of Javan: Elishah[a], Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.

signals.text: Genesis 10:4 reads “Dodanim” instead of “Rodanim,” reflecting a textual variation in the name.

source_text: בְּנֵ֣י שֵׁ֔ם עֵילָ֣ם וְ/אַשּׁ֔וּר וְ/אַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד וְ/ל֣וּד וַ/אֲרָ֑ם וְ/ע֥וּץ וְ/ח֖וּל וְ/גֶ֥תֶר וָ/מֶֽשֶׁךְ׃ס
english_snapshot: The sons of Shem: Elam[a], Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram; Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.

signals.text: Genesis 10:23 reads “Mash” instead of “Meshech” in the parallel genealogy.

source_text: מִשְׁמָ֣ע וְ/דוּמָ֔ה מַשָּׂ֖א חֲדַ֥ד וְ/תֵימָֽא׃
english_snapshot: Mishma[a], Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema.

signals.text: Genesis 25:15 has 'Hadar' in the parallel list; 1 Chronicles reads 'Hadad.'

source_text: בְּנֵ֖י אֱלִיפָ֑ז תֵּימָ֤ן וְ/אוֹמָר֙ צְפִ֣י וְ/גַעְתָּ֔ם קְנַ֖ז וְ/תִמְנָ֥ע וַ/עֲמָלֵֽק׃ס
english_snapshot: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman[a], Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna[b], and Amalek.

signals.text: Hebrew Zephi; Genesis 36:11 has the variant form Zepho.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֥י לוֹטָ֖ן חֹרִ֣י וְ/הוֹמָ֑ם וַ/אֲח֥וֹת לוֹטָ֖ן תִּמְנָֽע׃ס
english_snapshot: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam[a]; and Lotan’s sister was Timna.

signals.text: In the parallel genealogy at Genesis 36:22, the name appears as Hemam rather than Homam.

source_text: בְּנֵ֥י עֲנָ֖ה דִּישׁ֑וֹן וּ/בְנֵ֣י דִישׁ֔וֹן חַמְרָ֥ן וְ/אֶשְׁבָּ֖ן וְ/יִתְרָ֥ן וּ/כְרָֽןס׃ס
english_snapshot: The sons of Anah: Dishon. And the sons of Dishon: Hamran[a], Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.

signals.text: A parallel genealogy in Genesis 36:26 reads 'Hemdan' instead of 'Hamran.' The main text follows the Masoretic Text of 1 Chronicles here.

source_text: וַ/יָּ֨מָת֙ בַּ֣עַל חָנָ֔ן וַ/יִּמְלֹ֤ךְ תַּחְתָּי/ו֙ הֲדַ֔ד וְ/שֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖/וֹ פָּ֑עִי וְ/שֵׁ֨ם אִשְׁתּ֤/וֹ מְהֵיטַבְאֵל֙ בַּת מַטְרֵ֔ד בַּ֖ת מֵ֥י זָהָֽב־׃
english_snapshot: Baal-hanan died[a], and Hadad reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pai, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred[b], daughter of Mezahab.

signals.text: Genesis 36:39 gives the city name as 'Pau,' while Chronicles reads 'Pai.'

source_text: וַ/יָּ֖מָת הֲדָ֑ד וַ/יִּהְיוּ֙ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עליה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽתס׃
english_snapshot: Hadad died[a], and the chiefs of Edom were: Chief Timna, Chief Aliah[c][b], Chief Jetheth.

signals.text: Genesis 36:40 has the corresponding name as 'Alvah.' Chronicles here reads 'Aliah.'

source_text: וַ/אֲבִיגַ֕יִל יָלְדָ֖ה אֶת עֲמָשָׂ֑א וַ/אֲבִ֣י עֲמָשָׂ֔א יֶ֖תֶר הַ/יִּשְׁמְעֵאלִֽי־׃
english_snapshot: Abigail bore Amasa[a], and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and the parallel in 2 Samuel 17:25 read 'Ithra the Israelite' instead of 'Jether the Ishmaelite.' The Masoretic Text here reads 'Jether the Ishmaelite.'

source_text: וְ/כָלֵ֣ב בֶּן חֶצְר֗וֹן הוֹלִ֛יד אֶת עֲזוּבָ֥ה אִשָּׁ֖ה וְ/אֶת יְרִיע֑וֹת וְ/אֵ֣לֶּה בָנֶ֔י/הָ יֵ֥שֶׁר וְ/שׁוֹבָ֖ב וְ/אַרְדּֽוֹן־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Caleb son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah his wife[a], and by Jerioth; and these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab[b], and Ardon.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'her sons.' Some interpreters understand the genealogy differently, but the Masoretic Text has a feminine singular suffix here.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֤י כָלֵב֙ אֲחִ֣י יְרַחְמְאֵ֔ל מֵישָׁ֥ע בְּכֹר֖/וֹ ה֣וּא אֲבִי זִ֑יף וּ/בְנֵ֥י מָרֵשָׁ֖ה אֲבִ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן־׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn[a], who was the father of Ziph[b], and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.

signals.text: Hebrew syntax in the final clause is difficult. The Masoretic Text reads literally, 'and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.' Some understand this to mean 'Mareshah the father of Hebron,' while others retain the wording as translated.

source_text: וְ/אֵ֥לֶּה נוּלְּדוּ ל֖/וֹ בִּ/ירוּשָׁלָ֑יִם שִׁ֠מְעָא וְ/שׁוֹבָ֞ב וְ/נָתָ֤ן וּ/שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה לְ/בַת שׁ֖וּעַ בַּת עַמִּיאֵֽל־־־׃
english_snapshot: These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea[a], Shobab, Nathan[b], and Solomon—four by Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel.

signals.text: Hebrew Shimea; the parallel in 2 Samuel 5:14 has Shammua.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֣י פְדָיָ֔ה זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל וְ/שִׁמְעִ֑י וּ/בֶן זְרֻבָּבֶל֙ מְשֻׁלָּ֣ם וַ/חֲנַנְיָ֔ה וּ/שְׁלֹמִ֖ית אֲחוֹתָֽ/ם־׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei[a]. And the sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah; and Shelomith was their sister.

signals.text: Hebrew reads singular 'the son of Zerubbabel.' Because the verse then names Meshullam and Hananiah, many understand this as a textual irregularity or as genealogical usage functioning collectively; hence 'the sons of Zerubbabel' in the main text.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֥י שְׁכַנְיָ֖ה שְׁמַעְיָ֑ה וּ/בְנֵ֣י שְׁמַעְיָ֗ה חַטּ֡וּשׁ וְ֠/יִגְאָל וּ/בָרִ֧יחַ וּ/נְעַרְיָ֛ה וְ/שָׁפָ֖ט שִׁשָּֽׁה׃
english_snapshot: And the sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. And the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush[a], Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six.

signals.text: The Hebrew text says 'six,' though only five names are listed here in the Masoretic Text. This may reflect a textual issue or an omitted name in transmission.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֣י אֶלְיוֹעֵינַ֗י הדיוהו וְ/אֶלְיָשִׁ֡יב וּ/פְלָיָ֡ה וְ֠/עַקּוּב וְ/יוֹחָנָ֧ן וּ/דְלָיָ֛ה וַ/עֲנָ֖נִי שִׁבְעָֽה׃ס
english_snapshot: And the sons of Elyoenai: Hodaviah[a], Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven.

signals.text: The Hebrew spelling of the first listed name is unusual. 'Hodaviah' follows the most likely conventional identification; possible alternatives include 'Hodiah' or a more phonetic transliteration such as 'Hodevahu.'

source_text: וּ/בֶן עֶזְרָ֔ה יֶ֥תֶר וּ/מֶ֖רֶד וְ/עֵ֣פֶר וְ/יָל֑וֹן וַ/תַּ֨הַר֙ אֶת מִרְיָ֣ם וְ/אֶת שַׁמַּ֔י וְ/אֶת יִשְׁבָּ֖ח אֲבִ֥י אֶשְׁתְּמֹֽעַ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Ezrah: Jether[a], Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and she conceived Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah[c][b], the father of Eshtemoa.

signals.text: Hebrew literally, 'And the son of Ezrah.' Because several names follow, the phrase is commonly understood collectively as 'the sons of Ezrah.'

source_text: בְּנֵ֖י שִׁמְע֑וֹן נְמוּאֵ֣ל וְ/יָמִ֔ין יָרִ֖יב זֶ֥רַח שָׁאֽוּל׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Simeon: Nemuel[a], Jamin, Jarib, Zerah[c][b], and Shaul.

signals.text: Zerah corresponds to Zohar in the parallel genealogy of Genesis 46:10 and Exodus 6:15.

source_text: וְ/אֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת בְּֽנֵי גֵרְשׁ֖וֹם לִבְנִ֥י וְ/שִׁמְעִֽי־׃
english_snapshot: These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei[a].

signals.text: Hebrew manuscripts here read Gershom; some English traditions use Gershon in related genealogical contexts.

source_text: בְּנֵ֖י קְהָ֑ת עַמִּינָדָ֣ב בְּנ֔/וֹ קֹ֥רַח בְּנ֖/וֹ אַסִּ֥יר בְּנֽ/וֹ׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son[a], Korah his son, Assir his son.

signals.text: Some compare parallel genealogies where the corresponding ancestor is named Izhar rather than Amminadab; the Hebrew text here reads Amminadab.

source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֧י שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל הַ/בְּכֹ֥ר וַשְׁנִ֖י וַ/אֲבִיָּֽה׃ס
english_snapshot: And the sons of Samuel: the firstborn[a], Vashni, and Abijah.

signals.text: Hebrew Vashni. The phrase may also be understood as 'and the second'; compare 1 Samuel 8:2, which names Samuel's sons as Joel and Abijah.

source_text: וְ/אֶת עָשָׁן֙ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔י/הָ וְ/אֶת בֵּ֥ית שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶֽׁי/הָ־־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: Ashan with its pasturelands[a], and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands.

signals.text: Some parallel witnesses and translations list 'Ain' instead of 'Ashan' here; the Masoretic Text of Chronicles reads 'Ashan.'

source_text: וּ/מִֽ/מַּחֲצִית֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת עָנֵר֙ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔י/הָ וְ/אֶת בִּלְעָ֖ם וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑י/הָ לְ/מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת לִ/בְנֵי קְהָ֖ת הַ/נּוֹתָרִֽים־־־־־׃פ
english_snapshot: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner with its pasturelands[a], and Bileam with its pasturelands, for the clan of the remaining sons of Kohath.

signals.text: Hebrew Bileam; the parallel in Joshua 21:25 reads Ibleam.

source_text: וְ/אֶת חוּקֹק֙ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔י/הָ וְ/אֶת רְחֹ֖ב וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶֽׁי/הָ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: and Hukok with its pasturelands[a], and Rehob with its pasturelands.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Hukok.' The parallel in Joshua 21:31 has 'Helkath.'

source_text: לִ/בְנֵ֣י מְרָרִי֮ הַ/נּוֹתָרִים֒ מִ/מַּטֵּ֣ה זְבוּלֻ֔ן אֶת רִמּוֹנ֖וֹ וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֑י/הָ אֶת תָּב֖וֹר וְ/אֶת מִגְרָשֶֽׁי/הָ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: To the sons of Merari who remained[a], from the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono and its pasturelands, Tabor and its pasturelands.

signals.text: Hebrew reads 'Rimmono'; the parallel in Joshua 21:35 has 'Dimnah.'

source_text: וַ/אֲחֻזָּתָ/ם֙ וּ/מֹ֣שְׁבוֹתָ֔/ם בֵּֽית אֵ֖ל וּ/בְנֹתֶ֑י/הָ וְ/לַ/מִּזְרָ֣ח נַעֲרָ֔ן וְ/לַֽ/מַּעֲרָ֗ב גֶּ֤זֶר וּ/בְנֹתֶ֨י/הָ֙ וּ/שְׁכֶ֣ם וּ/בְנֹתֶ֔י/הָ עַד עַיָּ֖ה וּ/בְנֹתֶֽי/הָ־־׃
english_snapshot: Their holdings and settlements were Bethel and its daughter towns[a], and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its daughter towns, and Shechem and its daughter towns[c][b], as far as Ayyah and its daughter towns.

signals.text: The Hebrew text reads 'Ayyah'; some ancient witnesses and translations instead reflect 'Gaza.'

source_text: עוּתַ֨י בֶּן עַמִּיה֤וּד בֶּן עָמְרִי֙ בֶּן אִמְרִ֣י בֶן בני/מן בְּנֵי פֶ֖רֶץ בֶּן יְהוּדָֽה־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Uthai son of Ammihud[a], son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, from the sons of Perez son of Judah.

signals.text: Hebrew textual tradition here is difficult; the word rendered 'Bani' may alternatively be read 'from,' which would yield: 'son of Imri, from the sons of Perez son of Judah.' The main text follows the genealogical-name reading because it best fits the sequence of names.

source_text: וּ/מִן בְּנֵ֖י בִּנְיָמִ֑ן סַלּוּא֙ בֶּן מְשֻׁלָּ֔ם בֶּן הוֹדַוְיָ֖ה בֶּן הַ/סְּנֻאָֽה־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And from the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam[a], son of Hodaviah[c][b], son of Hassenuah.

signals.text: The name Hodaviah is spelled differently in some related genealogical traditions.

source_text: וּ/בְ/גִבְע֛וֹן יָשְׁב֥וּ אֲבִֽי גִבְע֖וֹן יעואל וְ/שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖/וֹ מַעֲכָֽה־׃
english_snapshot: In Gibeon lived Jeiel the father of Gibeon[b][a], and his wife's name was Maacah.

signals.text: The name is also spelled 'Jeuel' in some representations of the Hebrew; compare the parallel in 1 Chronicles 8:29.

source_text: וּ/בֶן יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן מְרִ֣יב בָּ֑עַל וּ/מְרִי בַ֖עַל הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת מִיכָֽה־־־׃
english_snapshot: And the son of Jehonathan was Merib-baal[b][a], and Merib-baal fathered Micah.

signals.text: Hebrew spells the father's name in two slightly different forms in this verse: 'Merib-baal' and a shortened form 'Meri-baal.' The translation regularizes the name for clarity.

source_text: וְ/אָחָז֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת יַעְרָ֔ה וְ/יַעְרָ֗ה הוֹלִ֛יד אֶת עָלֶ֥מֶת וְ/אֶת עַזְמָ֖וֶת וְ/אֶת זִמְרִ֑י וְ/זִמְרִ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת מוֹצָֽא־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Ahaz fathered Jarah[a], and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.

signals.text: The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 8:36 reads 'Jehoaddah' instead of 'Jarah.' The Chronicles manuscripts here read 'Jarah,' which is retained in the main text.

source_text: וְ/אַבְשַׁ֣י אֲחִֽי יוֹאָ֗ב ה֤וּא הָיָה֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הַ/שְּׁלוֹשָׁ֔ה וְ/הוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת חֲנִית֔/וֹ עַל שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל ו/לא שֵׁ֖ם בַּ/שְּׁלוֹשָֽׁה־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Abishai[a], the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three. He brandished his spear against three hundred slain[c][b], and had a name among the Three.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'the Three.' In the parallel passage (2 Sam 23:18), some English versions render the group differently because of textual and contextual difficulties involving 'three' and 'thirty.'

source_text: שַׁמּוֹת֙ הַ/הֲרוֹרִ֔י חֶ֖לֶץ הַ/פְּלוֹנִֽי׃ס
english_snapshot: Shammoth the Harorite[a], Helez the Pelonite[b];

signals.text: In the parallel list at 2 Samuel 23:26, the designation is 'the Harodite.' Chronicles here reads 'the Harorite.'
In the parallel list at 2 Samuel 23:26, Helez is called 'the Paltite.' Chronicles here reads 'the Pelonite.'

source_text: בְּנֵ֗י הָשֵׁם֙ הַ/גִּ֣זוֹנִ֔י יוֹנָתָ֥ן בֶּן שָׁגֵ֖ה הַ/הֲרָרִֽי־׃ס
english_snapshot: the sons of Hashem the Gizonite[a], Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite;

signals.text: The Hebrew text reads 'the sons of Hashem the Gizonite.' The parallel list in 2 Samuel 23:32 has a different name sequence, often reflected in translations or reconstructions.

source_text: חֵ֚פֶר הַ/מְּכֵ֣רָתִ֔י אֲחִיָּ֖ה הַ/פְּלֹנִֽי׃ס
english_snapshot: Hepher the Mecherathite[a], Ahijah the Pelonite[b],

signals.text: Or “the Paltite,” following the parallel reading in 2 Samuel 23:26 rather than the Masoretic wording here.

source_text: וְ/יִבְחָ֥ר וֶ/אֱלִישׁ֖וּעַ וְ/אֶלְפָּֽלֶט׃
english_snapshot: Ibhar[a], Elishua[b], and Elpelet.

signals.text: In the parallel account at 2 Samuel 5:16, the corresponding name appears as 'Elishama' rather than 'Elishua.' Chronicles here reads 'Elishua.'

source_text: בְּ/כֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּ/כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲ/דָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת אַחַד֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתִי לִ/רְע֥וֹת אֶת עַמִּ֖/י לֵ/אמֹ֑ר לָ֛/מָּה לֹא בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖/י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: In all the places where I have walked among all Israel[a], did I ever speak a word to one of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, ‘Why have you not built for me a house of cedar?’

signals.text: The parallel passage in 2 Samuel 7:7 reads 'tribes of Israel' (with some witnesses reflecting 'leaders' or 'scepters') rather than 'judges of Israel.' Chronicles' Hebrew text here reads 'judges.'

source_text: וּ/מִי֙ כְּ/עַמְּ/ךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גּ֥וֹי אֶחָ֖ד בָּ/אָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הָלַ֨ךְ הָ/אֱלֹהִ֜ים לִ/פְדּ֧וֹת ל֣/וֹ עָ֗ם לָ/שׂ֤וּם לְ/ךָ֙ שֵׁ֚ם גְּדֻלּ֣וֹת וְ/נֹרָא֔וֹת לְ/גָרֵ֗שׁ מִ/פְּנֵ֧י עַמְּ/ךָ֛ אֲשֶׁר פָּדִ֥יתָ מִ/מִּצְרַ֖יִם גּוֹיִֽם־׃
english_snapshot: And who is like your people Israel[a], one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, to make for yourself a name by great and fearsome deeds, driving out nations from before your people[b], whom you redeemed from Egypt?

signals.text: Hebrew 'driving out nations from before your people'; some understand the final word order differently because the parallel in 2 Samuel 7:23 is textually difficult.

source_text: וַ/יַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ צוֹבָ֖ה חֲמָ֑תָ/ה בְּ/לֶכְתּ֕/וֹ לְ/הַצִּ֥יב יָד֖/וֹ בִּֽ/נְהַר פְּרָֽת־־־׃
english_snapshot: David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah[b][a], as he went to establish his power at the Euphrates River.

signals.text: The name is spelled 'Hadadezer' here; the parallel in 2 Samuel 8:3 has the variant form often rendered 'Hadarezer.'

source_text: וַ/יִּלְכֹּד֩ דָּוִ֨יד מִמֶּ֜/נּוּ אֶ֣לֶף רֶ֗כֶב וְ/שִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ פָּֽרָשִׁ֔ים וְ/עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וַ/יְעַקֵּ֤ר דָּוִיד֙ אֶת כָּל הָ/רֶ֔כֶב וַ/יּוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖/נּוּ מֵ֥אָה רָֽכֶב־־׃
english_snapshot: David captured from him 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers. Then David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left from them enough for 100 chariots.

signals.text: 2 Samuel 8:4 has '1,700 horsemen' rather than '7,000 horsemen.' This is a parallel-passage numerical difference in the textual tradition.

source_text: וַ/יִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֗יד אֵ֚ת שִׁלְטֵ֣י הַ/זָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֔וּ עַ֖ל עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר וַ/יְבִיאֵ֖/ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
english_snapshot: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem[a][b][c].

signals.text: Some textual traditions and the parallel in 2 Samuel spell the name 'Hadarezer.'

source_text: וְ/צָד֧וֹק בֶּן אֲחִיט֛וּב וַ/אֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּן אֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִ֑ים וְ/שַׁוְשָׁ֖א סוֹפֵֽר־־׃
english_snapshot: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests[a], and Shavsha was secretary.

signals.text: The parallel in 2 Samuel 8:17 reads 'Ahimelech son of Abiathar' rather than 'Abimelech son of Abiathar.' The translation follows the Hebrew text of Chronicles here.

source_text: וַ/יָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִ/לִּ/פְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַ/יַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜יד מֵ/אֲרָ֗ם שִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְ/אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וְ/אֵ֛ת שׁוֹפַ֥ךְ שַֽׂר הַ/צָּבָ֖א הֵמִֽית־׃
english_snapshot: And Aram fled before Israel[a], and David killed seven thousand chariot warriors from Aram and forty thousand foot soldiers[b], and he put Shophach the commander of the army to death.

signals.text: The parallel passage in 2 Samuel 10:18 reads 'seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen.' Chronicles here reads 'seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers.'

source_text: וַ/תְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ/יַּ֞ךְ אֶלְחָנָ֣ן בֶּן יעור אֶת לַחְמִי֙ אֲחִי֙ גָּלְיָ֣ת הַ/גִּתִּ֔י וְ/עֵ֣ץ חֲנִית֔/וֹ כִּ/מְנ֖וֹר אֹרְגִֽים־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And there was war with the Philistines again[a], and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver’s beam.

signals.text: The parallel in 2 Samuel 21:19 has a difficult Hebrew text and is often discussed in relation to this verse; Chronicles explicitly says Elhanan killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.

source_text: לִ/ידוּת֑וּן בְּנֵ֣י יְדוּת֡וּן גְּדַלְיָ֡הוּ וּ/צְרִ֡י וִֽ֠/ישַׁעְיָהוּ חֲשַׁבְיָ֨הוּ וּ/מַתִּתְיָ֜הוּ שִׁשָּׁ֗ה עַל֩ יְדֵ֨י אֲבִי/הֶ֤ם יְדוּתוּן֙ בַּ/כִּנּ֔וֹר הַ/נִּבָּ֕א עַל הֹד֥וֹת וְ/הַלֵּ֖ל לַ/יהוָֽה־׃ס
english_snapshot: Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun—Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six—under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre in giving thanks and praise to Yahweh.

signals.text: The Hebrew text lists five names here but then says 'six.' Some interpreters infer that another son is omitted from the list, or that Jeduthun himself is counted.
